items.title: Allahabad High Court verdict denying right to wear hijab in school not a precedent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently said that the Allahabad High Court's August 21 judgment upholding a school's ban on wearing a hijab in classrooms shall not be treated as a precedent [ Muslim Womens Study Circle vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi made the observation while issuing notice to the State of Uttar Pradesh on a an appeal challenging the High Court verdict. The Court tagged the matter with the pending batch of appeals arising out of the Karnataka hijab ban case . "Permission to file the petition is granted. Issue notice. Tag with Civil Appeal No. 7095/2022 and this judgment shall not be treated as precedent," the Bench recorded in its November 20 order. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi The appeal before the apex court was filed against the High Court's August 21 judgment, which had upheld a school's classroom ban on headscarves while ruling that wearing a hijab is not an essential religious practice in Islam. items.title: New anaemia data raise questions over progress of Anaemia Mukt Bharat
items.summary: Months after releasing the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS) factsheet without crucial data on anaemia, the Union government has finally published the figures under a separate study. They were released on Tuesday, November 24, in a study titled the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023–2025. The data show that nearly 56% of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) are anaemic, despite a systematic intervention through Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB), a strategy launched in 2018. The Union Ministry, however, said that severe anaemia was observed only in less than 2% of people in the majority of the age groups. The report was prepared by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. While the government claimed that the prevalence of anaemia came down, experts point out that results of SAMPADA are not comparable with previous national surveys. An analysis of the Union Government’s scheme Anaemia Mukt Bharat, against the backdrop of survey results, shows nearly half of the funds remain unutilised. items.title: Supreme Court likely to pronounce verdict in Sabarimala reference case by December this year
items.summary: A nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court is likely to deliver its verdict in the Sabarimala reference case by December 18 this year. The case concerns seven larger legal questions on the scope of religious freedom in India. Justice BV Nagarathna, one of the judges on the bench, hinted that the verdict may be delivered before the Court closes for Christmas vacation on December 18. The indication came during the hearing of petitions challenging a High Court ruling on the Knanaya Catholic community’s alleged practice of expelling members who do not follow endogamous marriage customs. Since the Sabarimala verdict is likely to have a bearing on the Knanaya case, the Court proceeded to adjourn the matter and posted it for consideration in January next year. The Sabarimala reference was heard by a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant along with Justices BV Nagarathna , MM Sundresh , Ahsanuddin Amanullah , Aravind Kumar , Augustine George Masih , Prasanna B Varale , R Mahadevan and Joymalya Bagchi. items.title: Tamil Nadu introduces 15-day paternity leave for government employees
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday, November 26 announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male government employees, marking the first time that the state has introduced such a provision. The leave can be availed either 15 days before the birth of a child or within six months from the date of birth. An official government release said the decision was taken following requests from government employees. The new provision is intended to enable fathers to support their wives during childbirth and participate in the care and upbringing of their newborn children. The government highlighted the importance of a father’s involvement during the period surrounding childbirth, noting that both the mother and the newborn require support and care. The official release stated, “The period surrounding childbirth is crucial for both the mother and the child, and the father’s involvement in providing physical and emotional support to the mother and caring for the newborn is essential.” The announcement comes against the backdrop of the existing maternity leave provision for women government employees in Tamil Nadu, who are entitled to 365 days of maternity leave.
